::: {.lead-panel}
## Literature behind the analytical roadmap

This curated set connects the team's shared papers to decisions in the study. **Reviews orient the field; methods papers justify feasibility; neither substitutes for validation in ulcerative colitis.** Publisher and DOI links are used instead of redistributing article PDFs.
:::

## Start with the reviews

:::: {.evidence-grid}
::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-type}
REVIEW · CONCEPTUAL FOUNDATION
:::
### Fragmentomics, methylation, and tissue of origin

Lo and colleagues explain why cfDNA fragment size, end motifs, nucleosome organization, topology, and methylation can reveal aspects of tissue of origin [@lo2021fragmentomics]. It is the clearest foundation for treating the physical fragment and its methylation state as complementary measurements.

**Use here:** define the feature families and the biological interpretation boundary.
:::

::: {.evidence-card}
::: {.evidence-type}
REVIEW · TRANSLATIONAL LANDSCAPE
:::
### Fragmentomics in cancer

Tsui, Jiang, and Lo review current fragmentomic features, sequencing and computational approaches, clinical studies, and unresolved standardization questions [@tsui2025fragmentomics].

**Use here:** prioritize reproducible exploratory outputs; do not transfer cancer classifier performance to UC.
:::
::::

## Methods and proof-of-concept papers

| Paper | What it contributes | How it changes this project | Main limitation here |
|---|---|---|---|
| EM-seq from low-input DNA [@vaisvila2021emseq] | Enzymatic methyl sequencing at single-base resolution, including comparisons using cfDNA | Supports the assay choice and strict insert-size/library QC | Technical performance is not clinical validity |
| FRAGMA [@zhou2022fragma] | Links CpG methylation to cfDNA cleavage profiles and end motifs | Motivates exploratory fragment-end and methylation-aware summaries | Developed in other biological and disease settings |
| FinaleMe [@liu2024finaleme] | Infers methylation and tissue-of-origin signals from cfDNA fragmentation patterns | Provides a computational precedent for joint fragmentomic–epigenomic analysis | Its WGS model is not automatically transferable to EM-seq data |
| Plasma cfDNA methylation in SLE [@liu2025sle] | Demonstrates genome-wide cfDNA methylation analysis in an inflammatory autoimmune disease | Reinforces the need to distinguish inflammation-associated signal from neoplasia | SLE biology and the published assay/model differ from UC |

## Colombian genomics context

The CÓDIGO consortium illustrates the value of local genomics infrastructure, bioinformatics capacity, and ancestry-aware interpretation in Colombia [@marinoramirez2025codigo]. It does **not** provide a methylation reference panel for this study, but it strengthens the rationale for transparent provenance and locally relevant validation.

## Databases and reproducible resources

- [KEGG PATHWAY](https://www.genome.jp/kegg/pathway.html): manually curated molecular interaction and reaction maps for pathway interpretation.
- [Reactome Pathway Browser](https://reactome.org/PathwayBrowser/): curated human pathways and hierarchical pathway context.
- [NCI Genomic Data Commons](https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/): harmonized cancer genomic data, including TCGA resources for external triangulation.
- [NEB EM-seq tools and example data](https://github.com/nebiolabs/EM-seq/): implementation resource associated with the EM-seq method paper.

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this evidence"}
Evidence from oncology, SLE, or public cancer datasets can support feasibility, select features, and test biological coherence. It cannot directly validate prediction of UC progression. That requires a sufficiently powered, longitudinal, independent cohort.
:::
